name: Giotto
best_known_for: First close-up images of a cometary nucleus — flew 596 km past Halley's Comet on 1986-03-14 at 68 km/s, survived the dust impacts, then went on to encounter comet Grigg-Skjellerup in 1992
credit: ESA's first deep-space probe. Spin-stabilised drum-shaped bus protected by a Whipple-shield dust bumper (Kevlar + aluminum), built around the Halley Multicolour Camera, plus 9 other instruments contributed by 11 European countries + NASA + Japan. Closest approach to 1P/Halley was 1986-03-14T00:03 UTC at 596 km on the sunward side — the bumper survived but a 100 mg dust impact 14 seconds before closest approach offset the spin axis and broke camera contact. Recovered after the encounter, hibernated 1986-1990, then woke for a 200 km flyby of 26P/Grigg-Skjellerup on 1992-07-10 — the first time a spacecraft was reactivated for a second mission target. Final shutdown 1992-07-23.
